record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: Can combining senolytics with ROCK inhibitors and 5-LOX inhibitors contribute to tissue rejuvenation?

evidence.quote: Can a combination of senolytics with ROCK inhibitors and 5-LOX inhibitors contribute to tissue rejuvenation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Senolytics are pharmacological agents that selectively induce apoptosis in senescent cells (cells that have permanently exited the cell cycle and acquired a senescence-associated secretory phenotype). ROCK (Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinase) inhibitors are compounds that block the ROCK1/ROCK2 serine/threonine kinases, which regulate actin cytoskeleton dynamics, cell contractility, and tissue stiffness. 5-LOX (5-lipoxygenase) inhibitors are compounds that block the enzyme catalyzing the first committed step in the biosynthesis of leukotrienes from arachidonic acid, thereby reducing pro-inflammatory leukotriene signaling.

Determine whether a combination therapy that simultaneously administers (i) one or more senolytic agents, (ii) one or more ROCK inhibitors, and (iii) one or more 5-LOX inhibitors can produce measurable tissue rejuvenation in aged mammalian tissues — meaning a restoration of structural and functional properties (e.g., regenerative capacity, stem-cell function, extracellular matrix composition, reduced chronic inflammation, improved tissue mechanics) toward those characteristic of younger tissues — beyond the effect of any single component or pairwise combination. Provide either an experimental demonstration of such synergistic rejuvenation (in vivo, with appropriate aged controls) or a principled argument that no such combined effect can be achieved.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open biomedical research question posed as part of a roadmap of unanswered problems in biogerontology. No published study appears to demonstrate the specific triple combination (senolytics + ROCK inhibitors + 5-LOX inhibitors) producing tissue rejuvenation; individual classes have been studied separately for senescence clearance, fibrosis/stiffness reduction, and inflammation reduction, but the combined effect remains unverified.

status_evidence.snippet: Listed among open questions in combination rejuvenation therapy.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an unsolved open problem in a 2025 roadmap of biogerontology.
